slides.title: FM-VLA: Force-based Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models in Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.highlight: FM-VLA introduces a force-based memory system using a VAE to encode force histories, allowing VLAs to reason about temporal context in visually ambiguous, contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: FM-VLA uses force-based memory to enable temporal reasoning for non-Markovian, contact-rich robotic manipulation tasks.
card.key_idea: A pretrained VAE compresses long-horizon wrench histories into compact memory tokens, combined with short-term proprioceptive state tokens, to condition a flow-matching action expert.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three bimanual tasks (finding blocks, pressing buttons, wiping dishes); achieved 83.3% average success rate, significantly outperforming memoryless and vision-memory baselines.
card.limitation: The fixed 8-token VAE bottleneck may be insufficient for very long-horizon tasks requiring memory of hundreds of contact events.

slides.title: Towards Artificial Nerves: Biomimetic Optical-Fiber Tactile Sensing for Robots
slides.highlight: OptiTac emulates human mechanoreceptor architecture using optical fibers to provide high-resolution, interpretable tactile sensing for robotic manipulation.

card.one_liner: OptiTac is a biomimetic tactile sensor using optical fibers to enable interpretable, high-resolution robotic touch.
card.key_idea: Pairs each mechanical pin on soft skin with one optical fiber, routing signals to a remote camera for analytical processing via image moments.
card.evaluation: Tested with various indenters; achieved sub-millimeter localization (RMSE ~0.4mm), linear contact-width estimation, and 96% shape classification accuracy using GMMs.
card.limitation: Performance was validated under controlled laboratory conditions with short fibers; robustness to long-distance routing and environmental variation remains unquantified.

slides.title: Representation-Aligned Tactile Grounding for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Latent Tactile Predictor that aligns intermediate action representations with future contact consequences to improve VLA policies in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: Improves contact-rich robotic manipulation by grounding VLA policies using future tactile prediction at intermediate representations.
card.key_idea: Uses linear probes to identify intermediate action-expert features as the optimal interface for a Latent Tactile Predictor (LTP) that predicts compact future tactile embeddings.
card.evaluation: Tested on five real-world tasks using SmolVLA and π0 backbones; achieved 74% and 73% average success, outperforming VLM-side and final-state grounding.

slides.title: Never Too Late for Force: Accelerating VLA Post-Training with Reactive Force Injection
slides.highlight: LIFT introduces a force-aware post-training framework that injects 6D end-effector force into VLA policies, enhancing contact-rich manipulation. This aligns with MOSAIC's focus on physics/force-based skill acquisition and human-AI coadaptation.

card.one_liner: LIFT adds reactive force sensing to pretrained VLAs to improve contact-rich manipulation via online post-training.
card.key_idea: Grafts a reactive action expert with causal force memory and zero-initialized cross-attention, coupled with an online DAgger loop to mitigate force distribution shift.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on towel folding, book insertion, and Hanoi ring placement; LIFT outperformed vision-only DAgger and single-frame force baselines in success rates.
card.limitation: Depends on human corrections during online DAgger, limiting data throughput; evaluated only on single-arm manipulation.

slides.title: Catch, Throw, Repeat: Planning for Human-Robot Partner Juggling
slides.highlight: This work presents a planning and control architecture for synchronized multi-ball juggling, advancing physical human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A real-time planning system enabling a robot to perform synchronized multi-ball partner juggling with humans.
card.key_idea: Integrates predictive ball tracking, adaptive online trajectory optimization via multiple-shooting, and state-machine-based coordination logic to manage catch-and-throw decisions in real-time.
card.evaluation: User study with 8 participants (beginner to expert); achieved 3-ball cascades and 100% success in single-ball trials; results exceed previous records.
card.limitation: Performance is constrained by timing pressure at high ball counts and lack of explicit inter-ball collision avoidance.

slides.title: VTAP Gripper: Synergizing Fingertip Sensing and a Visuo-Tactile Active Palm for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
slides.highlight: This research introduces a gripper combining a visuo-tactile active palm with tactile array sensors to achieve robust grasping and fine manipulation without high-DOF anthropomorphic designs.

card.one_liner: A tactile-reactive gripper using an active bi-modal palm for dexterous in-hand manipulation and teleoperation.
card.key_idea: Integrates a 13-DOF structure with fingertip tactile arrays and an actuated palm that switches between visual localization and tactile feedback via controllable internal illumination.
card.evaluation: Tested on YCB objects, syringe reorientation (65% success), object singulation (down to 3mm), and peg-in-hole insertion (70% success) using VR teleoperation.
card.limitation: VR hand-tracking occlusions can cause unintentional grasp release during complex motions, such as depressing a plunger.

slides.title: MIDAS Hand: Modular low-Impedance Direct-drive Anthropomorphic Sensing Hand
slides.highlight: The MIDAS Hand provides a low-impedance, anthropomorphic platform with integrated tactile sensing, supporting human-to-robot data collection relevant to MOSAIC's focus on human proficiency and skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: A low-cost, open-source, human-scale dexterous hand featuring direct-drive actuation and dense tactile sensing.
card.key_idea: Combines 13 active DoFs, 3D-printed modular construction, and 283 three-axis tactile taxels with low-friction, directly-driven actuation for compliant, anthropomorphic manipulation.
card.evaluation: Validated via GRASP taxonomy (32/33 types), backdrivability tests (≈0.02 Nm), payload tests (>9.5kg), and 5,000+ cycle reliability tests. Results appear robust.
card.limitation: Lacks a little finger, limiting certain ulnar-side grasps; tactile sensing is not yet integrated into closed-loop control.

slides.title: BayesContact: Uncertain Pose Estimation via Visuo-Tactile Proposals and Simulation-based Inference
slides.tldr: VISUO-TACTILE POSE ESTIMATION VIA SIMULATION-BASED INFERENCE
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework for visuo-tactile pose estimation that fuses depth observations with contact evidence, contributing to the multimodal perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: BayesContact uses simulation-based inference to fuse visual and tactile data for precise peg-in-hole pose estimation.
card.key_idea: A Sequential Monte Carlo framework that updates a particle belief using rendering-based depth likelihoods and physics-based contact likelihoods derived from force/torque measurements and guarded probing.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation and real-robot experiments across five geometries; improved pose observability and insertion success by 30% over vision-only inference.
card.limitation: Likelihood evaluations during the contact phase require physics simulations, preventing the use of Metropolis-Hastings rejuvenation for particle refinement.
